children: Rozebud Gonsalves Mumbai: The 10-year government bond yield has boxed itself into a narrow 6-8 basis points (bps) range this week as dealers refrain from taking fresh positions ahead of next week's monetary policy decision amid ostensibly conflicting incoming data inputs involving consumer inflation and oil price trends. One basis point is a hundredth of a percentage point. "Traders do not typically keep very large positions before an event that is very uncertain, because it gets difficult to contain the volatility after the announcement.

Yields suddenly move 5-6 bps, leaving no chance to exit; hence traders tend to trim their positions," said Alok Singh, head of treasury, CSB Bank. The latest narrow trading band follows a sharp reversal in yields, which climbed to 7.50% in October before retreating to 7.07% earlier this month, where the weekly range of yields was between 33 basis points to 17 basis points, CCIL data showed.

The benchmark yield closed at 7.23% on Thursday, up seven basis points from its previous close, with movements largely tracking fluctuations in crude oil prices. While a 25-basis-point rate hike is already priced in, any hawkish commentary from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor next Friday could push yields towards 7.30%, treasury heads said. The price action in bond yields on Thursday reflected the increase in crude oil prices, which again raises concerns on India's import bill.

The 10-year yield increased seven basis points. "A day with a seven-bps yield movement is quite volatile, when you compare it with stable days of 2-3 bps move. Higher oil prices can reverse the gains we have seen in November," said a bond trader at a private sector bank. Brent crude futures were trading at $93.79 a barrel at around 3PM, from around $90 the previous day, according to Reuters.

A sustained rise in oil prices can widen the current account deficit, put downward pressure on the rupee and feed into domestic inflation, as India is a large importer of the commodity. "Crude price is the biggest driver of the commodity, because otherwise positions are slim ahead of the policy," said VRC Reddy, head of treasury, Karur Vysya Bank. If there is hawkish commentary from the RBI, then a move to 7.30% is likely," he said.

title: Yield Band Narrows ahead of Rate Call
